text:
jamie: Weekly capacity forecast: quick read + hotspot triage. Key asks: confirm EU buffer for model-v2 rollout, decide APAC preemptible cap, and agree on throttling for background rerank.

ravi: looked at the telemetry — EU peak climbed to ~94% on Tue 09:00 UTC, forecast suggests 97-99% Wed morning if rollout continues. Main pressure from chat-sqr workload (~1.8k GPU hours/day).

maria: APAC (apac-sg1) seeing ~15% preemptible churn this week; fallback to us-west adds ~120ms median latency. That fallback is also driving up egress costs (small but visible).

noah: quick regional snapshot I pulled:
- eu-north-1: current 72 GPUs, forecast peak need ~86 GPUs; with 20% buffer target -> target pool ~103-107 GPUs.
- us-west-2: current 120 GPUs, forecast peak ~105 GPUs (we're overprovisioned there by ~15%).
- apac-sg1: current 40 GPUs, forecast peak ~55 GPUs (preemptible risk).

tina: can we reduce pressure by switching rerank and some batch to quantized-8? Early tests showed ~25-35% GPU hour savings on rerank models.

ravi: +1 on the quantization pilot. Also shifting low-priority batch to region-local night windows (~02:00 local) can buy ~4-6% runway in each region.

maria: ops-bot flagged a network egress cap event in eu-north-1 at 10:12 UTC yesterday — saw short TCP stalls in zone-b that delayed KV cache warmups. Link: https://internal/reports/egress/17549 (logs attached in the incident channel).

deploy-bot: Canary for model-v2 started in eu-north-1 @2024-11-06T08:30Z, traffic 12% -> ramp paused due to latency tail at p95.

jamie: Decision point: allocate +16 reserved GPUs in eu-north-1 (monthly cost delta ~ $11.8k) OR slow the canary and shift some traffic to the dedicated pool. Reserve gives runway for SLA but increases burn. Thoughts?

noah: If we reserve, we hit SLA headroom and keep rollout pace. If we instead route to other regions, median improves but p95 may get worse depending on egress congestion. Quick sim: prefer eu-west fallback before apac reduces added latency to ~60ms vs apac fallback ~120ms, but increases cross-region egress cost.

maria: proposal: temporary policy -> prioritize critical-latency routes (chat, real-time) and throttle background rerank when region util > 85%. That reduces peak demand while keeping critical traffic stable.

tina: implemented a throttle config prototype; snippet below (ready for quick deploy):

```
route:
  name: rerank-background
  throttle:
    max_rps: 60
    window: 60s
    spill_to: low-priority-pool
```

ravi: Action items: 1) jamie approve throttle rule -> tina to deploy. 2) noah run cost simulation for reserved GPUs vs egress routing by EOD. 3) maria run preemption trend + batch-shift plan for APAC. 4) tina run a small quant-8 canary for rerank in eu and apac.

jamie: I approve the throttle rule rollout now. Hold on reserving GPUs until we see noah's cost sim. Also greenlight a tiny quantization canary (5% traffic) in eu-north-1 and apac-sg1.

maria: noted — I'll run the cost sim and post results here (will include monthly burn, egress delta, and latency impacts).

ops-bot: Forecast alert: projected weekly GPU hours +18% over baseline for next two weeks if current rollout continues without mitigation.

noah: quick sim summary (preliminary):
- reserve +16 GPUs eu-north-1 -> +$11.8k/mo, meets SLA, p95 improves ~8-12ms.
- egress-routing alternative -> +$3.2k/mo in egress, p95 increases ~20ms on average for some fallbacks but median latency stays acceptable.
- quantization pilot estimated savings ~30% GPU hours on rerank workload (~0.4k GPU hours/day saved if fully rolled).

ravi: thanks. If cost sim favors egress route, plan = deploy throttle, configure eu-west fallback, shift batches to night. If reserve is cheaper given SLA, we approve reservation.

jamie: OK. I'll follow up in tomorrow AM sync with the final call. Thanks all — great triage. :thumbsup:
